# vphone-cli > Looking for vphone-cli 1.x? See the [1.0.14 release](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/tag/1.0.14). Create and run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac. vphone-cli uses Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research VM infrastructure. Version 2.x applies the complete firmware patch set, including changes previously offered as EXP. There are no selectable patch variants. The self-contained `VPhone.bundle` handles firmware preparation, restore, and VM control; `vphone-launchpad` installs the bundle and guides you through creating and running a VM. The recommended host setup runs `csrutil enable --without debug` and `csrutil allow-research-guests enable` in macOS Recovery. SIP remains enabled with debugging restrictions relaxed. Launchpad checks the host and uses its privileged helper to allow each verified VM binary through AMFI; see [host setup](Documents/Guides/host-setup.md) for details. ## Get started Use the notarized [vphone-launchpad 2.0.8](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/download/2.0.8/vphone-launchpad-2.0.8-notarized.zip) on a physical Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or newer. The release needs no Xcode, Python, or Homebrew at runtime. 1. In macOS Recovery, run `csrutil enable --without debug` and `csrutil allow-research-guests enable`, then restart. See [host setup](Documents/Guides/host-setup.md) for details. 2. Unzip and open the app. Complete **Host Setup**, including Developer Tools access and installation of the privileged helper. 3. In **Core Bundle**, choose **Download and Install** for the latest `VPhone.bundle`. Launchpad verifies the download and prepares its VM binary for the host. 4. In **Machines**, choose **New Machine**, select a firmware pairing from the catalog, and click **Create**. Launchpad completes the first-boot check and leaves the VM running. Catalog pairings download firmware. Creating a VM needs network access for restore tickets and substantial free disk space, even with local IPSWs. You can supply your own compatible iPhone and cloudOS IPSWs. See [compatibility](Documents/Guides/compatibility.md) for verified pairs. For source builds and terminal workflows, see [host setup](Documents/Guides/host-setup.md) and [create and run](Documents/Guides/create-and-run.md). Version 2.x starts only VMs created with its `schemaVersion=2` format. Older VMs must be recreated. ## Custom Firmware Bootstrap After launching the VM, choose **Guest > Install Bootstrap…** from the macOS menu bar and select a layout. This installs Irisin in the guest. For the first setup, select `apt` and `bash` in Irisin. Press and hold the **Install** button, then choose **Bootstrap Install**. This mode unpacks all packages in the installation before running the installation steps again. It resolves the initial dependency cycle where `debianutils` needs `bash`, but `bash` needs `debianutils` to have been configured. Use regular installation after this setup is complete. ## Everyday use The VM window provides app and file browsing, clipboard and preference tools, screenshots, recording, and diagnostics. For local automation, launch with `--api-listen 127.0.0.1:8765`. The VM prints a new API token at each launch as `[api] token: …`, or uses `VPHONE_API_TOKEN` when you set it. Send the token with every request, for example `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/health`. Requests without the token are refused, and so are requests from web pages. See the [guest API](Research/vphoned_http_api.md). | Task | Command | | --- | --- | | List VMs | `vphone-cli vm list` | | Inspect a VM | `vphone-cli vm info myphone` | | Start the VM window | `vphone-cli vm launch myphone` | | Stop a VM | `vphone-cli vm stop myphone` | | Export a backup | `vphone-cli vm export myphone --out myphone.tzst` | | Import a backup | `vphone-cli vm import myphone.tzst --name restored` | VMs live under `~/.vphone/` by default. Run `vphone-cli --help` for more commands. ## How it fits together `vphone-cli` prepares firmware, restores VMs, and manages their lifecycle. The bundled `vphone-vm` runs the guest and owns its macOS window. Inside the guest, `vphoned` provides the controls used by the window and the optional HTTP and WebSocket API. The `VPhone` Xcode scheme builds and validates the self-contained `VPhone.bundle`. ## Repository map | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | [`VPhoneExecutable/`](VPhoneExecutable/) | CLI, VM process, firmware patcher, and restore backend | | [`VPhoneKit/`](VPhoneKit/) | Shared host libraries and API client | | [`VPhoneDaemon/`](VPhoneDaemon/) | Guest control daemon, `vphoned` | | [`VPhoneGuestComponents/`](VPhoneGuestComponents/) | Guest hooks and support binaries | | [`Documents/`](Documents/README.md) | Setup, usage, compatibility, and troubleshooting guides | | [`Research/`](Research/README.md) | Patch and implementation notes | ## Acknowledgements - [wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup](https://github.com/wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup)

releases.name: v2.0.8
releases.body:
## vphone 2.0.8

- Rename the bundled AMFI helper executable to `vphone-escalator`. Launchpad and standalone setup commands now use this name.
- Require VPhone.bundle 2.0.8 or newer in Launchpad. Older installed bundles remain removable, but cannot be selected or used; there is no fallback to the old helper name.
- Fix the Irisin bootstrap installation alert so a completed download stays at 100% and late status polls cannot reset it.
- Align the bootstrap alert status text and progress bar with the alert body using equal 22 pt left and right padding.

Upgrade Launchpad and install the 2.0.8 Core Bundle together. The separately distributed Launchpad app is available as a notarized download below.

releases.name: v2.0.6
releases.body:
# vphone-cli 2.0.6

This release fixes VM cloning and boot-state preservation. It follows [2.0.5](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/tag/2.0.5).

## Get started

Download the [notarized vphone-launchpad 2.0.6](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/download/2.0.6/vphone-launchpad-2.0.6-notarized.zip), unzip it, and replace the previous app. In **Core Bundle**, choose **Download and Install** to install `VPhone.bundle` 2.0.6. The [bundle archive](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/download/2.0.6/VPhone-2.0.6.zip) is also available for CLI use.

## Fixes

- `vm clone` now copies the complete VM folder, using APFS copy-on-write when available and a regular folder copy otherwise. It preserves the machine identifier, NVRAM, SEP storage, SHSH blobs, and other boot state. Clones keep the same device identity; change it manually if needed.
- VM launch now opens an existing NVRAM file instead of recreating and overwriting it. This preserves boot tickets across launches. A new NVRAM file is created only when none exists.
- Launchpad's Clone sheet now accepts its suggested clone name immediately. The outdated warning about resetting the clone's identity has bee

releases.name: v2.0.5
releases.body:
# vphone-cli 2.0.5

Version 2.0.5 hardens the trust boundaries around the Launchpad helper, the root CFW install and the guest agent. It also improves location simulation and adds a few conveniences to the VM window. This note covers the changes since [2.0.4](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/tag/2.0.4).

## Get Started

Download the **[notarized vphone-launchpad 2.0.5](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/download/2.0.5/vphone-launchpad-2.0.5-notarized.zip)**, unzip it, and open the app. If Launchpad is already installed, replace it with this version, then choose **Download and Install** in **Core Bundle** to install `VPhone.bundle` 2.0.5. The [Core Bundle asset](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/releases/download/2.0.5/VPhone-2.0.5.zip) is available if you use `vphone-cli` directly.

Host requirements are unchanged. See the [README](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli#readme) and [host setup](https://github.com/Lakr233/vphone-cli/blob/main/Documents/Guides/host-setup.md) if you are setting up a new Mac.

## Security

A repository-wide security review found issues in the root CFW install, the Launchpad helper, VM bundle handling and the guest boundary.

Docs · 中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

vphone-cli

Looking for vphone-cli 1.x? See the 1.0.14 release.

Create and run a virtual iPhone on an Apple Silicon Mac. vphone-cli uses Apple's Virtualization.framework and PCC research VM infrastructure.

Version 2.x applies the complete firmware patch set, including changes previously offered as EXP. There are no selectable patch variants. The self-contained VPhone.bundle handles firmware preparation, restore, and VM control; vphone-launchpad installs the bundle and guides you through creating and running a VM.

The recommended host setup runs csrutil enable --without debug and csrutil allow-research-guests enable in macOS Recovery. SIP remains enabled with debugging restrictions relaxed. Launchpad checks the host and uses its privileged helper to allow each verified VM binary through AMFI; see host setup for details.

Get started

Use the notarized vphone-launchpad 2.0.8 on a physical Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or newer. The release needs no Xcode, Python, or Homebrew at runtime.

  1. In macOS Recovery, run csrutil enable --without debug and csrutil allow-research-guests enable, then restart. See host setup for details.
  2. Unzip and open the app. Complete Host Setup, including Developer Tools access and installation of the privileged helper.
  3. In Core Bundle, choose Download and Install for the latest VPhone.bundle. Launchpad verifies the download and prepares its VM binary for the host.
  4. In Machines, choose New Machine, select a firmware pairing from the catalog, and click Create. Launchpad completes the first-boot check and leaves the VM running.

Catalog pairings download firmware. Creating a VM needs network access for restore tickets and substantial free disk space, even with local IPSWs. You can supply your own compatible iPhone and cloudOS IPSWs. See compatibility for verified pairs. For source builds and terminal workflows, see host setup and create and run.

Version 2.x starts only VMs created with its schemaVersion=2 format. Older VMs must be recreated.

Custom Firmware Bootstrap

After launching the VM, choose Guest > Install Bootstrap… from the macOS menu bar and select a layout. This installs Irisin in the guest.

For the first setup, select apt and bash in Irisin. Press and hold the Install button, then choose Bootstrap Install. This mode unpacks all packages in the installation before running the installation steps again. It resolves the initial dependency cycle where debianutils needs bash, but bash needs debianutils to have been configured. Use regular installation after this setup is complete.

Everyday use

The VM window provides app and file browsing, clipboard and preference tools, screenshots, recording, and diagnostics. For local automation, launch with --api-listen 127.0.0.1:8765. The VM prints a new API token at each launch as [api] token: …, or uses VPHONE_API_TOKEN when you set it. Send the token with every request, for example curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/health. Requests without the token are refused, and so are requests from web pages. See the guest API.

Task Command
List VMs vphone-cli vm list
Inspect a VM vphone-cli vm info myphone
Start the VM window vphone-cli vm launch myphone
Stop a VM vphone-cli vm stop myphone
Export a backup vphone-cli vm export myphone --out myphone.tzst
Import a backup vphone-cli vm import myphone.tzst --name restored

VMs live under ~/.vphone/ by default. Run vphone-cli <group> --help for more commands.

How it fits together

vphone-cli prepares firmware, restores VMs, and manages their lifecycle. The bundled vphone-vm runs the guest and owns its macOS window. Inside the guest, vphoned provides the controls used by the window and the optional HTTP and WebSocket API. The VPhone Xcode scheme builds and validates the self-contained VPhone.bundle.

Repository map

Path Contents
VPhoneExecutable/ CLI, VM process, firmware patcher, and restore backend
VPhoneKit/ Shared host libraries and API client
VPhoneDaemon/ Guest control daemon, vphoned
VPhoneGuestComponents/ Guest hooks and support binaries
Documents/ Setup, usage, compatibility, and troubleshooting guides
Research/ Patch and implementation notes

Acknowledgements

  • wh1te4ever/super-tart-vphone-writeup

aiSummary.oneLiner: A command-line tool for interacting with VirtualPhone, enabling automated management of virtual iOS devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: vphone-cli provides a terminal-based interface and automation toolkit for managing VirtualPhone instances (a platform for running virtualized iOS devices). It bridges the gap between the VirtualPhone GUI and automated CI/CD workflows by allowing developers to programmatically control device lifecycles. Users can use the CLI to create, start, stop, and snapshot virtual iPhones, as well as install applications, push files, and execute shell commands inside the virtual environment. This abstraction is critical for teams that need to integrate iOS testing, security analysis, or app deployment into headless scripts without relying on manual interaction.
keyFeatures: Device lifecycle management: Commands to boot, shutdown, and reset virtual iOS devices.
App installation: Sideload IPA files directly into the virtual environment from the command line.
File system interaction: Push and pull files between the host machine and the virtual device.
Snapshot control: Create and restore device states for reproducible testing scenarios.
Shell execution: Run commands directly within the virtual iOS environment.
CI/CD integration: Designed for headless operation within automated testing pipelines.

useCases.title: Automated iOS testing
useCases.description: QA engineers use the CLI in CI/CD pipelines to spin up a clean virtual iPhone, install a new build, and run tests.

useCases.title: Security research
useCases.description: Security analysts script the rapid deployment and teardown of specific iOS versions for vulnerability analysis.

useCases.title: App reverse engineering
useCases.description: Researchers use the tool to automate the extraction of app data and memory dumps from virtualized devices.

useCases.title: Headless device management
useCases.description: DevOps teams manage fleets of virtual iOS devices on remote servers without requiring graphical access.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This tool is built for iOS developers, QA automation engineers, and security researchers who need programmatic control over virtualized iOS environments. It requires access to VirtualPhone and familiarity with command-line interfaces.
